_comment: Which runtime lane a Session gets, and why. The single source for the
decision order, the device tiers, the reason codes and the failure
outcomes; scripts/test-apple-profile-policy-contract.sh checks the Swift
mirrors against it.
Two rules hold over everything below and are not negotiable:
1. The profile is frozen before any content code runs, and never changes
for the life of the Session. The lanes do not share a JavaScript heap,
a renderer, or resource ownership, so there is no lossless switch at
runtime. What reads as 'falling back' is either a choice made before
user code ran, or a reload under a new runtime generation.
2. Every decision carries a reason. The question production actually
asks is never 'which lane' but 'why did this device, on this content,
end up there' -- and by the time it is asked, the inputs are gone.

Reasoning: this file once mirrored fixed byte caps copied from another vendor's device tiers, and they were withdrawn -- no public API reports the jetsam limit, so a cached number is not a budget but a guess wearing one. What remains is a policy expressed as inputs and rules, which is why every field here names a signal to read rather than a threshold to trust. The record of that decision is in the maintainers' notes, which are not part of this distribution.

decision_order.note: An explicit host choice is honoured or refused outright. The low-level C ABI takes a resolved profile and never guesses; only the Host Kit offers 'auto'.
Whether this binary contains the lane at all. Reported from what the artifact actually compiled, never from what the enum can name.
Against lanes.*.min_os in deployment-floor.json. Necessary, never sufficient.
What the content declares it needs, and which profiles it declares it was built for. Content that never declared a lane does not get it.
The runtime checks that cannot be inferred from a version number: crossOriginIsolated, a working Atomics.wait round trip, ANGLE device creation. A probe that cannot run is a failure, not a pass.
OS build and GPU combinations known to be broken. Data, shipped separately from the binary.
The kill switch. Takes effect on the next Session, never mid-run.
Repeated failures on this device and content demote the lane. Advisory: it can only make the choice more conservative.
The last gate, and the only one that runs after resources are committed. It must complete before any content code executes, so a failure here still selects rather than falls back.

memory_policy._comment: These inputs combine verified content and host caps, measured device-safe evidence, fresh available-memory advisory headroom, and a versioned emergency reserve. Effective admission uses the most conservative current inputs; the advisory is re-queried before large reservations, and no value is a jetsam limit or guarantee.

content_cap.note: Verified content-manifest cap supplied as a runtime input.

host_cap.note: Host-provided cap supplied as a runtime input.

measured_device_safe_cap.note: Device-model, OS, and build evidence selects this safe cap at runtime.

available_memory_headroom.note: Applied after a fresh os_proc_available_memory() query before a large reservation; never cached as a maximum.

emergency_reserve.note: Versioned policy input reserved for emergency recovery.

_comment: Tiers gate the fast lane. They do not gate the product: a device below
T1 runs ios_webkit_full, which is a supported configuration and not a
degraded one. Collapsing 'this device cannot run Performance+' into
'this device is unsupported' is the mistake that cost 2.4 points of
coverage in the superseded design.

T0.conditions: iOS below the Performance+ minimum, or under 3 GB of RAM, or denylisted, or a failed capability probe
T0.note: Compatibility-lane admission and conservative content quality; this tier does not define a runtime memory cap.

T1.conditions: at or above the Performance+ minimum OS, at least 3 GB of RAM, capability probe passed
T1.note: Performance+ admission and standard content quality; runtime memory is selected from current observations.

T2.conditions: T1, plus a GPU family that supports the higher texture and resolution variants
T2.note: Performance+ admission with higher asset quality; the quality tier does not change runtime memory policy.

_comment: What happens to the Session that hit the failure, and what the next one
gets. Two columns because they are different questions: a running
Session cannot change lane, so the current column is always about
stopping cleanly and the next column is where the choice is made.

transport_init_failed.current_session: fail before any content code runs

wire_validation_failed.current_session: terminate the content and record a security event
wire_validation_failed.next_session: do not retry the same bundle; disable remotely

sustained_backpressure.current_session: lower the quality tier and pause the producer; terminate only past a hard limit
sustained_backpressure.next_session: ios_webkit_full if the limit was reached

webcontent_terminated.current_session: void the generation, drop unacknowledged packets, show recovery UI
webcontent_terminated.next_session: rebuild the same lane, or ios_webkit_full if it recurs

renderer_init_failed.current_session: fall back before content code runs

device_or_context_lost.current_session: stop accepting packets, advance the resource epoch, rebuild recoverable resources
device_or_context_lost.next_session: same lane; a new Session only on repeated failure

memory_critical.current_session: drop caches, lower the tier, pause uploads; exit in order if still short
memory_critical.next_session: same lane at a lower tier

jit_unavailable.current_session: run correctly and record the capability

shader_cache_corrupt.next_session: same lane; a cache fault is not a lane fault

feature_flags._comment: Default state on a fresh install. Anything not 'on' requires device evidence to promote, and every one of them must be switchable off remotely without a client update.
